fixes.why: What a prime number is counts as school arithmetic, which this part assumes. Proof by contradiction (p178) also uses primes without teaching them.
The open need for p180 names both 'if and only if' and the converse. N188 links to p147, and p147 only needs p145, so the converse (p146) has to be added as its own link.
p203 only needs the school idea of an infinite decimal, and it says the rigorous version comes later. Linking it to the real-numbers part would make this part need a later one, which is backwards.
Cantor's theorem is proved by contradiction (assume a surjection onto P(A) exists, then look at the diagonal set), but nothing on its chain of needs reaches proof by contradiction.

verdict: The part is sound and complete for its brief. The five pieces fit together without real duplication, and nearly every open need is met by a point already in another piece, so no new points were needed. After linking the open needs and adding two missing cross-piece needs, the dependency structure holds together. Two needs were dropped as school knowledge: primes and decimal expansions.
